Founded in the sixteenth century during the Mạc Dynasty, the pagoda was originally constructed on the site of the former residence of the revered Prince Linh Lang, adding a layer of historical significance to its tranquil ambiance.

Founded in the sixteenth century during the Mạc Dynasty, the pagoda was originally constructed on the site of the former residence of the revered Prince Linh Lang, adding a layer of historical significance to its tranquil ambiance. The name "Tào Sách" evokes a poetic essence, recalling the ancient tradition of early morning literary discussions and poetic recitations among the prince and his scholarly companions.

The pagoda's massive three-entrance gate, built from dark lim wood, is adorned with moss-covered curved tiles, adding to its serene ambiance. The gate's architecture is a testament to the ingenuity and craftsmanship of the artisans who built it, and its majestic bell tower on the second floor is a symbol of the pagoda's spiritual significance.
